reports.title: OGTT 22 Jan
narrative: They don’t call it the Ocean’s Greatest Time Trial for nothing, and the first OGTT of 2026 wasted absolutely no time reminding us why.

We were greeted on arrival by a big-eyed Q-Ball, who, in an impressive display of pre-race commitment, managed to end up on the rocks before the race had even started. A strong opening act, and one that set the tone beautifully for what followed.

Conditions were… character building. A howling north-easterly screamed straight into our faces, while on the beach the Commodore delivered the briefing: a leisurely stroke out, followed by a flat-out 4,000-metre race back to the beach. Simple in theory. Less so in practice.
The paddle out was filled with lively banter, though anyone who’s done PE to East London was clearly having vivid, unwanted flashbacks as the headwind did its best to crush spirits and posture alike.

At the 4,000-metre mark, batches were sent off at one-minute intervals. And then….chaos. Everyone launched like men possessed, paddles flying, dignity optional. Unfortunately for them, no one could live with my blistering pace.

I hit the beach first, but it wasn’t over yet. Out came the running shoes as I effectively sprinted from four poles to the steps in what can only be described as an absolutely world-class finish. Textbook. Clinics will be run.
Turning back to admire the carnage, the scene was biblical. Boats scattered along the shoreline like driftwood after a storm. Some more unlucky than others.

A special shout-out to Ty, who somehow managed to break yet another boat. A rare talent. Thankfully, he’s off to Pretoria soon, where he’ll have absolutely no need for any paddling equipment whatsoever.
A fitting start to 2026. Same race. Same chaos. Same winners.

reports.title: OGTT Race Report  5 February 2026:
narrative: The Ocean’s Greatest Time Trial – Tiffany’s Beach Edition 06:00

For the first time in the history of this prestigious event, the OGTT was held as a morning edition - reasons unclear. Today the ocean rolled out the red carpet at Tiffany’s Beach for what can only be described as elite athletic excellence lightly disguised as chaos. The gun (okay, imaginary gun) went at Furby’s stairs, where a couple of swimmers warmed things up by pretending the shore break was a CrossFit obstacle course. Furby himself led by example, demonstrating—for the third day in a row—that there is absolutely nothing to fear except dignity in the shore break.

Conditions? Glorious. Proper postcard stuff. A couple of flyers punched out early like they were late for a meeting, while the rest of the field settled into an easy four kilometres offshore, generously seasoned with banter, unsolicited coaching, and deeply questionable pacing strategies.

The turnaround was highlighted by a debate on batches for a staggered start. Rob was ceremonially nominated as the rabbit. Released ahead of the pack and immediately pursued by a baying collection of hounds who smelt blood, bragging rights, and possibly coffee. With very little bump and zero free speed, the return leg was honest work—no charity runs, no gifts from the ocean. Every glide had to be earned the old-fashioned way: suffering quietly and pretending you’re loving it.
Into backline and the order at Furby’s stairs was locked in:
Skinny Cappuccino was disqualified for crimes against the sport, including not starting on time and taking the short course. Appeals will not be heard, mostly because nobody cares.
All in all: great ocean, great crew, minimal assistance, maximum effort, and exactly the kind of race that reminds us why we keep coming back.

reports.title: 23 April OGTT Race Report
narrative: The news from school that we would be finishing early on Thursday brought a real sense of excitement, knowing it meant I’d be lining up for the OGTT that afternoon. As a boarder in PMB, the OGTT is something I wish I could take part in every week, but logistically it doesn’t always work out—so when the opportunity presents itself, I really look forward to racing alongside some of KZN’s top paddlers.

I managed to get back to the North Coast in time, and the conditions couldn’t have been better. A light southerly made the launch easy, while still providing just enough assistance on the return leg to set up a fast, competitive run home. It was one of those days where everything aligned perfectly for racing.

The paddle out to the turn was relaxed, with the usual Tiff Tigers banter and a chance to catch up after a busy week. But as always, that changed the moment we hit the turn—the mood shifted instantly, ears pinned back and race mode fully engaged.

From there, it was full gas to the finish. The pace lifted quickly, the group began to stretch, and everyone pushed hard for position. In an unusual turn of events, Hank made a rare mistake coming into the finish, spinning out at a critical moment—something I don’t think anyone has seen from the legend before. That opened the door, and I was able to take full advantage, and luckily taking the win.
A special mention goes to Warren, who joined the session but unfortunately just missed the start.
All in all, a great afternoon on the water—good conditions, fast racing, and even better banter!

reports.title: 7 May - OGTT Race Report — Ocean’s Greatest Time Trial
narrative: The surf was up. Way up. Big enough that Emilio and Brad took one look at the swell, made some sensible noises about “responsibilities” and “not dying,” and stayed on dry land where the coffee is hot and the rescue boats unnecessary. We respect the decision. We also note it for the record.
That left a hardy — or possibly foolish — starting lineup of Zoog, Barry XS, Hank & Furbs, Qball, and Coffee.

Barry XS launched like he’d been shot out of a cannon, sprinting off the beach with a turn of speed that made Hamish look like he was paddling through treacle. Whether this was a tactical masterclass or pure adrenaline-fuelled panic remains unclear, but it was glorious to behold for the roughly ninety seconds it lasted.
Meanwhile, Coffee and Qball set off together at what can only be described as a leisurely pace, chatting away like two retirees on a dam outing.
The 4km out leg was completed by all parties as per race briefing — some with more conviction than others.

Handicaps were duly issued at the turn. Then it was a straight dash back to the beach, where the OGTT’s ancient and sacred principle was once again proven: simple math wins the day. No fancy strokes, no secret training programmes, no carbon wonder-skis required. Just arithmetic and a vague sense of direction.

Hank and Furbs take the win, proving that two heads are better than one — particularly when one of them can do sums. Zoog held it together for a respectable second. Qball edged out Barry XS, whose early sprint apparently used up his entire fuel allocation for the day. And Coffee rounds out the field, which is exactly where Coffee likes to be: last, but unbothered.

I’ll be signing your skis tomorrow.

reports.title: OGTT 02 July
narrative: Let’s start with the elephant in the room: the attendance. It seems a quick glance at Hurricanes favourite app today caused a sudden, mysterious spike in "hamstring niggles," "work emergencies," and "traffic." To the 5 brave souls who actually dragged their skis down to the beach: I salute you. To the rest of you clutching your heated blankets and watching Netflix: we missed you, but the ocean didn't.

Mother Nature woke up and didn’t chose violence to begin with according to the masses that completed a paddle this morning instead of joining us… however the Cobras head decided to quadruple in size in the space of 6 minutes. We were staring down sets that looked less like waves and more like moving apartment blocks. The wind was howling, and the launch zone was basically a washing machine. Perfect OGTT weather.
Navigating the Cobras Head was a sorting hat for who actually knows how to paddle and who just pretends on Strava.

It’s safe to say that no Strava pretenders rocked up this evening… Moses as always delivered for the 400th time in a row whilst the rest of us wrestled our way to backline, before setting off into some seriously dark clouds and a 30 knot fan.

This evening’s event was a fastest 1km event and it seems that the tactical move was a shorter route and more power… Julia and myself in the double proving that the old Ballies and their lines and tactics don’t always prevail.

Despite the chaos, the cream always rises to the top, even when the top is covered in sea foam. I navigated the mayhem with the grace of a dolphin and the speed of a man who just wanted to get to Siggis… Flip the Black Label was fresh!
NOTE: These times are based on previously agreed on handicaps.
To the handful of you who paddled out, it was an honor. To the no-shows, the handicaps will be brutally adjusted in your absence.
I’ll accept my congratulations in the form of beers next Thursday. Assuming the surf drops to a manageable .5 of a foot so the rest of you can join us again.

reports.title: OG-TT 19 June
narrative: Race Report: The Great Social Paddle Fiasco
(Now with 37% more confusion and 100% more beer)

At precisely 16h00, A Batch launched with military precision (if the military were made up of semi-retired surfers and part-time paddlers). B Batch followed bravely at 16h15, possibly under the impression they were in a completely different race — or time zone.

A Batch all made it out safely, which was a miracle considering some were still emptying his boat of water at the start line. We paddled off toward Sheffield like aquatic gladiators on a 4.5km odyssey of mild exertion and maximum gossip.

On arrival at the halfway point, the designated leader of A Batch — driven by hunger, thirst, or a deep distrust of B Batch’s timekeeping — decided that "waiting" was an outdated concept and led the fleet back to Tiffs. Democracy was voted against 1–0.
As for B Batch… I honestly have no idea what happened to them. They may still be out there. Paddle-powered and purpose-lost.

Meanwhile, A Batch, being absolute weapons, completed their 2000m sprint with grace, style, and one or two emotional breakdowns. We then hit the beach and made a tactical advance to Siggi’s — not for medals, but for draughts of golden glory.
Eventually, a few scattered and dehydrated members of B Batch stumbled in, presumably guided by the scent of beer and disappointment.

Now, as per Rule 17.42 of the Club Constitution — which was obviously drafted under the influence of several previous paddles — any member who fails to reach Siggi’s and consume at least one beverage is hereby DQ’d from the event. No exceptions. Not even for detoxing triathletes.
Therefore, please find attached the Updated Official Placings, reflecting not speed, nor endurance… but adherence to the sacred post-paddle pint.

reports.title: OG-TT 3 July
narrative: A warm welcome to Dom, Raul, and Jacques on their OGTT debuts.
The Race all began with what was supposed to be a race to the backline… which, in reality, was about as thrilling as a synchronised yawn.
From there, we glided into a breezy 4km paddle.
At the 4km mark, we turned, the pace lifted as a self-seeded free-for-all broke out. No gun, no line, just pure chaos — like Black Friday, but for mid-life paddlers.
Painting launched like a man possessed… unfortunately by poor judgment, he headed straight down QBall’s patented “line to nowhere” and gave himself about as much chance as a snowman in Durban.
Vern, showing rare tactical insight, joined us further offshore — a move that might have paid off, had he not turned the finish into a Cirque du Soleil audition.

Keegs looked dangerously sharp — clearly putting in the hours — but still needs to learn the art of shorebreak survival (note: maybe don’t take lessons from his dad). He’s all promise and paddle… but still under construction.
Warren and Brent were rock solid — dependable as ever — though comfortably outside the threat zone. More “classroom monitors” than competitors.

Kevin had a good session, though one gets the sense he was dreaming more about the post-paddle beers than the finish line. Once he revealed he went to Michaelhouse, everything suddenly became clear — paddling with champagne problems.

Raul, our visiting Dabs Navy Commander, nearly went full Titanic at the break but somehow managed to channel his inner fish. His Midmar Mile finish was the stuff of urban legend — or a low-budget NatGeo special. Either way, bravo.

reports.title: OG-TT 17 July
narrative: Tactical Brilliance, Tardy Dads & a Scrotum-Nibbling Garfish
Before I begin… a moment of silence, please, for Furby’s brand-new old boat.
May she rest in two pieces. I’ve always heard that two halves are better than one — especially when you're trying to double your warranty claims.

There was a protracted negotiation on course layout, race rules, form, and function before the whistle — essentially a committee meeting disguised as a paddle. This delayed the start and led to an almost dusky finish. The lack of clear direction from Commodore Zoog was dearly missed; turns out democracy at sea results in total anarchy.

The start itself was a confused affair. Those fading right — aka Heavy Right-Footed Painting — and the rudderless duo of my father and the Heidelberg Hitman, Damian Muller (debut appearance, DNF), found the backline as elusive as a coherent WhatsApp plan.
A yellow card was issued to Ralph for arrival tardiness — apparently, domestic duties (“the dishes”) took precedence over OGTT. A brave, if ill-advised, call.

The paddle to Christmas Bay was a casual cruise. Banter flowed freely, with Vern throwing in the occasional surge, revving the engine with gusto and leaving the rest of us scrambling like pensioners at a Black Friday sale.
Then came the turn. And away we go.

Batch A, B, and C received their respective “handicaps” — which in the end meant absolutely nothing as they crumbled beneath the weight of my tactical genius. It quickly became a two-horse race, punctuated briefly by a scrotum-nibbling garfish (yes, my mullet does have that effect — even on members of the animal kingdom).
The finish was chaos: exploding doubles, the odd swim, and some questionable navigational decisions. But all in all, a successful evening out.

reports.title: OG-TT 31 July
narrative: Vern “van Aert” Claims a Historic Maiden Victory in Iconic OG-TT Fashion
·        Wave Size: 2-3 ft with occasional 4 ft sets
·        Tide: Incoming high tide during mid-race
·        Weather: Scattered clouds – textbook OGTT conditions
Seven paddlers and one fisherman (Dr Gunning’s self-inflicted handicap) lined up on Tiffs Beach for another legendary edition of The Ocean’s Greatest Time Trial – and it did not disappoint.

As tradition dictates, the race began with the a Le Mans start, a mad dash from the dune to the skis and through the shorebreak. Lightee’s vintage skills got him through the surf quickly which resulted in a 300m lead to the first buoy.
Zoog, Painter and Furbs all had a solid start and were chasing hard while Vern rolled out of his ski and was frolicking in the shorebreak, trailing the group with a mountain of work ahead.

Brent, who nearly forgot the traditional pre-race pushups (again), fought valiantly to catch Clint at the end of the 1st lap. However, a mistimed entry through the mid-break led to a brutal swim and dropped him to 4th.

Clint held the lead into lap two, with Zoog hot on his heels, however a couple waves to Zoogs chest and he lost momentum just as Vern began to mount what is being referred to as "The Miracle of 2025." Into the headwind, Vern passed Zoog and chased down Clint as if he was dragging a kelp forest behind his rudder.

Vern turned the top buoy first, notoriously a weak downwinder, he needed nothing short of divine intervention to hold off Clint, Zoog and a charging Brent… and somehow he delivered. Vern turned the bottom buoy with a few seconds’ gap to spare. Behind him, Clint faltered, turning the buoy the wrong way in a heartbreaking navigational blunder that would ultimately disqualify him.
Vern came surging into Tiffs Beach, claiming his first-ever OGTT win — a result compared to Van Aert’s victory over Pogacar on the final stage of the Tour de France 2025.

Still breathless and choking back the tears Vern said “I’ve waited so long for this. To finally cross the line first... it means everything. To come back from a start like that? I thought I’d blown it. This one is for my family, they have supported me all these years”.

When asked about holding off Clint and Zoog on the downwind, Vern claimed “I’ve never beaten either of them in a downwind and I knew they were chasing hard. I just prayed and paddled like hell. Maybe it was a current, maybe it was magic — I don’t know. All I know is I finally did it.” (he laughs, then gets choked up again)
The 31 July edition of OGTT will go down as one of the most dramatic races in recent memory. A new champion has emerged — and his name is Vern van Aert.
Will he defend his crown next week? One thing’s for sure — no one’s taking him lightly ever again.

reports.title: OG-TT 7 Aug
narrative: It was cloudy. It was cold. It was raining. In short, it was the kind of weather that makes you question your life choices.
But OGTT does not cancel. Not for weather, not for war. So at 16:30 sharp, Zoog called it to order with all the military precision we are used to.
A small but committed crew gathered, shivering behind my garden wall like meerkats avoiding a tax audit.
It was agreed — after much debate (lasting 12 seconds) — that we’d embark on a 4km “social paddle” towards Ballito.
The staggered start was as follows:
The “cannon” went off — which in OGTT terms means Gunning just quietly paddled off while we pretended that was dramatic.
Zoog, bless him, launched like a rocket. 🚀
Then Brent went on his way.
Now, I was laser-focused. So focused, in fact, that I never saw Brent again.
Soon, it was a two-horse race: Team Furbs & Qball vs. Zoog.
Nerves of steel. Arms of jelly. But Qball was digging like a labrador on a beach, and somehow we reeled Zoog in.
Then came a magical wave. A glorious, foamy gift from Poseidon himself. We rode it like champions — or at least like two guys who really didn’t want to paddle anymore.
Victory was ours. Sweet, soggy, and completely undeserved.

reports.title: OGTT – 21 Aug - The Divide at Tiffs
narrative: Reported from San Diego, far, far away from the chaos, because yes… I had to escape the drama. 😎

Thursday at Tiffs started like any other… until the unthinkable: Tiger King Vern and Zook were AWOL. Panic. Chaos. And in a historic twist, a downwind course was declared — the “inclusive, no-surf-navigation-required,” perfect for anyone who prefers fun over ego.

Not everyone approved. The Elites Toti, Socks, and the “Rudderless Rogue” threw a collective tantrum, staging their own secret regatta away from the peasants. For their efforts? 1 point each for participation. Yes, that’s it.
Meanwhile, on the downwind, the true heroes emerged:
1.      Pips — powered by desperation, aerodynamic finesse, and sheer stubbornness.
2.      Hunk (Hank) — paddling like a superhero audition, smooth, strong, and still smiling.
3.      Furbs — master of the Tiffs holy grail spot. Every stroke screamed “local legend.”
4.      Picasso (Painting) — graceful and unpredictable, leaving spectators unsure if they were witnessing a race or a masterpiece.
5.      Chris A — the globe-trotting travel photographer, proving that capturing waves also requires paddling prowess.
The rest of the downwind paddlers, in no particular order:
·        B_Rad — casual, confident, possibly distracted by the scenery.

reports.title: OG-TT 4 September
narrative: ORDER RESTORED AT THE OCEANS GREATEST TIME TRIAL

It was a great day. It was a great day for surf ski paddling. It was a great day for the young man from Palm Lakka as he bludgeoned his way to glory, leaving a mist of calm and order in his tail slip just a week after what was beginning to resemble a scene out of a John Wick episode..

Zoog, resplendent in his Carbonology (Paid full price, zero sponsorship – just loves it) was faultless on the amended easterly course – 3 laps, touching the stairs on each lap – he was amazing this evening and is expected to get more than 8 likes on his Strava activity for this effort.

The rest of the event seemed rather processional. Always a few stories and excuses and rightly so a few highlights - Nikon & The Olympian just snuck ahead of Bench Press Barry who just slid in before Phelps the 2nd. It has been quietly noted by the eldership that Toti has had a disastrous last few outings and is looking likely to take complete ownership of the Phelps title should his luck and or skills not dramatically change..

4 Day work week was like an Oryx silhouetted against the setting sun in his Epic – a picture of grace, power and stature. He navigated numerous challenges on his Epic craft to secure valuable points on the log.

Dionn lead the last trio home with Waterboy narrowly missing out on the wooden spoon. Last across the line was Double Latte/Chin extra cream Cappucino – he will be hoping for an improved performance next week as he races Gunner and Tiger King in the most anticipated match up of the year…

reports.title: OG-TT 11 September
narrative: Billed by some in the lead up as possibly the most important race of the year (which is saying a lot given World Champs is next month), this evening’s Oceans’ Greatest Time Trial was one for the ages, the stuff of (Skinny’s) dreams, and Mother Nature delivered as promised.
The course was set, and the rules were simple enough: *“4:30 start at Westbrook, fastest 1km split will take victory.” *

There was lots of smack talk beforehand, but it was clear from the charts that the peak of the gusts was to arrive at 5pm (55kph), at an angle of 197’, lining up perfectly with Ballito point: all that remained was to get a few warm up runs in, and arrive at the turn, well rested by 5pm, then go full send. Simple. Like taking a Landcruiser from a baby. The rest is history.
The Jacobs’ appearances on the podium this week continued with Troy coming in second, beating Vern into 3rd (But solid performance given his jet lag and black lung).

Well done to all that participated, including the Retired Tigers and Dionn on his first outing. The rest of the results posted below for completeness. Special mention to Skinny on his 12th place finish today: good job.

reports.title: OGTT Race Report 09 Oct
narrative: We were greeted with excellent conditions today – full tide and a solid, punchy shorebreak. It was one of our biggest turnouts yet, with the Tiff Tigers sharpening their form ahead of the World Champs next week.
We were also privileged to be joined by two-time U23 and one-time Junior World Surf Ski Champion - Uli Hart.

Our fearless leader, Zoog, got us underway, sending the field charging headfirst into some sizeable shories. Imagine a swarm of overly-caffeinated penguins fleeing a hungry leopard seal – that was us, the Tiff Tigers, kicking off another classic OGTT.

Brent and Keegs started one minute behind the main pack, with Hank and Uli launching two minutes further back. Brent, battling a mysterious illness, couldn’t hold the pace for long, but Keegs surged through and soon reeled in the leaders. Hank and Uli were closing the gap fast, however Keegs picked the cleanest line to the beach, nailed the landing, and had a comfortable jog up to the stairs to take the win. Hank followed close behind for a strong second.
Another epic OGTT with the legendary Tiffs Tigers 🐅

reports.title: OG-TT 4 July
narrative: The wonderful west arrived mid morning giving the Tigers a chance to try their hand at a downwind TT. A well timed and convincing video of the easy looking launch at Westbrook was posted (may or may not have been filmed today), made sure that there was a good squad of paddlers ready to do battle on the coastal race course.
Getting to the start line proved very entertaining for the adoring crowds of wives and drivers as Barry “Big Waves Don’t Scare Me Painting” valiantly rode a foamy 50 metres backwards to the beach.
Then ensued a period of deep consideration for the Tiffs Tigers as the waves pounded the Westbrook sands.
Eventually the team launched in spits and spurts. The young guns making it look easier than the rest.

Most of the real entertainment was kindly provided by yours truly when a wave that proved of little consequence to Pilot  H. McGregor winded his passenger  and broke his paddle into two useless pieces.

A quick swim back through 3m waves to the sand to collect a fresh paddle (Thanks B.Lewin) and then back to the double was quickly and effortlessly undertaken without fear or exhaustion. H.McGregor entertained himself meanwhile by piloting his passenger less Surfski in the zone of death to pass the time.
Landing of the day goes to M.Gunning whose unwavering belief in his ability to outrun a mountain of water 5 times taller than himself over 300 metres is inspiring.
Captain VV landed like a professional Surfski paddler but it doesn’t count as he had already had a practice session this morning.

Keegan was also seen throwing in 300 press-ups post race at the Furby stairs to cover all  handicap complaints and avoid potential disqualification and Ty Haynes was overheard the parking lot considering training in a boat instead of with a 9 iron with Surfski SA Champs coming up. All in all though.. a splendid time was had by all.
1. Hank Mid Break Meditator McGregor and Chris Breaker Allan

reports.title: OG-TT 03 October
narrative: On October 3rd, the highly anticipated "Ocean's Greatest Time Trial" (OG-TT) took place under challenging yet exhilarating conditions. Paddlers were required to complete four laps of 3 kilometers each, coming ashore after every lap to touch the stairs before heading back out. The tricky northeast swell and accompanying wind presented significant challenges; however the downwind conditions gave the elite paddlers a chance to capitalize on their speed and wave-riding skills.

The time trial was raced at the peak of high tide, making the in-and-out transitions tricky and navigating the shore break required extra skill. Many paddlers took unplanned swims, adding an unpredictable element to the contest and spectators with some costly repairs expected to one boat in-particular.

The day marked a significant achievement for both Marco and Vern, who secured their debut wins in this prestigious event. Rumors circulated that this victory was the pinnacle of their paddling careers, and their performance certainly impressed spectators and fellow competitors alike. Despite the difficult conditions and three swims, Vern and Marco demonstrated exceptional speed as they managed to stay consistent and strong throughout the race.

Warren showed his class by keeping pace with the lead S2 most of the race, demonstrating superior wave skills. Zoog applied pressure on Warren, but an unfortunate early capsize in the shorebreak cost him a potential second-place finish. Despite the setback, Zoog remained competitive, showcasing his resilience throughout the race ending with a respectable 3rd. A welcome return saw Rich Rose secure a surprising 4th place in the S2 with Stoff. Their performance was solid, especially given Rich’s absence from competitive paddling.

The Ocean's Greatest Time Trial lived up to its name, offering a thrilling race that tested paddlers' endurance and technical skills. The paddling community eagerly awaits the next edition, with this week setting a high standard for both athleticism, drama and excitement.

reports.title: OG-TT 24 Oct
narrative: The storms earlier in the week had brought in some impressive swell, but the rain had finally stopped and the Tiffs Tigers were treated to a beautiful evening for ocean sport. The size and power of the surf would have resulted in any ICF sanctioned competition being postponed but were suitably testing for the Oceans Greatest Time Trial.

This evenings race began at Furby’s stairs with each paddler touching the newly installed sandbags. The course was 3 laps clockwise around the yellow boys off Villa Royale, coming in through the surf to touch the stairs on each lap, approximately 10km in total.

A slight error in judgement on my part coming in on the second lap left me swimming from back line and my boat in the mid break at 4 poles. Attempting to get back through the surf from here resulted in me getting my ski handed back to me at least 4 times, twice at my head. Thankfully 4 poles is too far down the beach for Carol’s camera.
The results I have were therefore kindly sent from Warren, as I was in no position to see who came in where, from so far back in the field:

reports.title: OGTT Diwali Edition 2024 – 31 Oct 2024
narrative: This evening, symbolic candles and sparklers flickered like our hopes for an easy race, celebrating the eternal victory of light over darkness (and hopefully avoid the shorebreak fireworks).

In a surprise twist, two old rivals decided to call a truce. Skinny and Male Nurse, known more for their mutual smack talk than for teamwork, teamed up for this Diwali edition to show us all that, when it really counts, humanity comes first. Or at least… tries to.

Off the line, the universe immediately conspired against them. Skinny’s bold choice of "wizard-sleeve" pants, with leg holes so wide they were practically cast nets, quickly proved to be a design flaw. The North Coast shorebreak was not impressed, as Skinny was left wrestling with his pants around his ankles in the surf. Flashbacks from decades past reportedly led Dr. Gunning to pick anesthesiology over proctology, once he realized that some sights cannot be unseen.

Despite these early setbacks, the pair managed an impressive start. They looked poised to take the lead—until they faced another pitfall: the dreaded 20 push-up penalty. The push-ups turned out to be the real finish line for them, and all hopes of victory drifted away like Skinny’s sagging waistband.

In a show of Diwali spirit (or maybe just overconfidence), Icarus—the dad with the most kids in town—decided to race on a spec ski, convinced that this was his moment to outshine us all. Spoiler alert: he flew too close to the sun.

After all the “festivities,” Skinny decided to treat the gang to a round of counter-culture hospitality! We all sipped on these “Small Portuguese” beers. Apparently, they make a size specifically for children's parties. In Skinny’s defense, it was well-received and totally on brand. Cheers, Skinny!
1.      Brent: Brought the heat, the skill, and maybe some luck... 1st place, fair and square.
2.      Double Trouble: Two heads (or dice rolls) are still better than one…
3.      Icarus what goes up must come 3rd.
4.      Super Mario: Showed up with swagger, left quickly.
5.      Sthututhu: Had the spirit of a lion, the luck of a kitten.
7.      Photographer: Seen floundering once or twice.
8.      Bushpig: Understated but undefeated in his own right. Managed to make it past midbreak this week.
AWOL/DNS: Qball, Spug spug, captain zoognut.
